title: Sequence-length-aware perplexity and oracle task scorer harness for quantized profiles
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: Build a robust, sequence-length-aware metric harness that (1) computes perplexity and token-level divergence for FP8/INT8 quantized profiles with per-layer calibration offsets, and (2) provides an "oracle" task-fidelity scorer that aggregates MMLU-style multi-choice accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE for generation tasks, and custom task-specific scorers (code correctness, instruction-following precision) into a unified failure budget. This harness will be the canonical evaluator used in calibration pipelines and release gating for quantized profiles.
background: Current quantization validation is fragmented: we have profile-level quality checks and several adhoc scorers (see ENG-4219, ENG-5372). Gaps observed in recent FP8 runs: significant perplexity variance at long sequence lengths, and task-level accuracy regressions not captured by global averages. Signal is noisy when sequence length and token distribution differ between calibration and production traffic. We need a single, extensible metric harness that is length-aware and supports task-level oracles and composite scoring for gating.
approach: 1) Implement a sequence-length bucketing layer: bucket test examples into short/medium/long chains and compute perplexity and token-KL per-bucket. 2) Add per-layer calibration diagnostics: record activation histograms and per-layer scaling offsets to correlate with delta-perplexity. 3) Create an 'oracle task scorer' that normalizes and composes: - MMLU-style accuracy and calibrated confidence; - BLEU/ROUGE for summarization/translation with length-normalized variants; - Code-task exact match and execution-based validators (sandboxed) with timeouts; - Instruction-following scorer based on structured output checks. 4) Expose fail budgets: absolute thresholds and percentile-based regression windows. 5) Integrate into existing calibration pipelines as an adapter so that CI/CD jobs can call it with a quant profile and receive structured pass/fail + diagnostic artifact links.
acceptance_criteria: Perplexity computed per sequence-length bucket (short/medium/long) for FP8 and INT8 runs and stored as timeseries in the metrics backend
Token-level KL and per-layer activation histograms produced for each profile run and linked in the run artifact
Oracle task scorer returns composite fidelity score and component breakdowns (MMLU accuracy, BLEU, ROUGE, code-exec success) for provided task suites
Regression gates implemented: pass/fail decision and detailed diagnostics (top N failing prompts, per-token divergence) for CI usage
Tooling integrated with calibration pipeline endpoint and runtime-1.25 release; example CI job and sample dataset in CI repo
Documentation and runbook for interpreting fail budgets and next-step remediation actions
tasks: Design metric schema + CI contract (oss: metric names, labels, bucket boundaries)
Implement sequence-length bucketer and perplexity module (Python), include streaming support for large corpora
Add per-layer activation histogram collector to profile runner and wire into artifact store
Implement oracle task scorer adapters: MMLU loader, BLEU/ROUGE wrappers, code-exec harness (sandbox wrapper), instruction-structure validator
Create composite scorer that normalizes component metrics and emits an overall fidelity score + component breakdown
Create CLI and REST adapter for the calibration pipeline to call scorer with a quant profile
Add dashboards: length-bucket perplexity timeseries, top-N failure prompts, per-layer anomaly heatmap
Write docs, runbook, and sample CI job; add unit and integration tests
Run initial validation suite on the FP8 baseline and produce a 'smoke' report
open_questions: What boundaries should we use for length buckets? (proposal: <=64, 65-512, 513-2048, >2048)
How should we weight different task types in the composite fidelity score? (equal-weight vs. production-weighted)
Do we run code-exec validators on every CI run or only on nightly/full-suite runs due to resource cost?
What percentile delta should trigger an automatic rollback in the calibration pipeline?
risks_mitigation: Risk: Code-exec validators are expensive and flaky. Mitigation: sandbox with strict timeouts and fall back to static checks for CI-level jobs; full dynamic checks in nightly runs.
Risk: Overfitting bucket boundaries to our current datasets. Mitigation: make bucket config data-driven and exposed as pipeline param; log distribution drift metrics.
Risk: Composite score hides component regressions. Mitigation: require component-level thresholds in addition to composite pass/fail.
Risk: Metric computation slows down CI. Mitigation: streaming compute and sample-based fast-path for quick PR checks; full-run in dedicated job.
